mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% in a single month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages over two months signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise above 12-month averages for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages for two months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise above 12-month moving averages for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed 12-month moving averages for three months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening labor market conditions, which supports consumer demand and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Real personal savings (RSAFS) persistently above their 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates elevated household savings relative to spending, which in a stable monetary regime typically foreshadows future consumption and investment, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS remains above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months in a stable monetary regime (t-test p > 0.10).
